# Verification: proving the engineering claims

Traceability is incomplete if requirements terminate at design. This chapter models verification as first-class engineering objects and connects successful tests to explicit evidence.

The test cases below correspond to real classes of regression checks in the repository. Twenty-three executable bindings now cover architecture-decision governance, multilingual semantic parity, public graph safety, named graph views, change impact, margin-TOC usability, the OSLC federation path (orchestration, reconciliation identity, bounded query, member observation, import plan), the GitHub issues adapter (identity, cache, pagination, reconciliation, rate limits), and extension-first distribution (clean render, offline reuse, version-skew isolation, corruption, concurrency, spaces in paths, Quarto floor). `make evidence-self-example` executes those tests, writes deterministic provider output, attests it against the current engineering snapshot, and validates `.quarto-needs/evidence/pytest.json` before the self-hosted book is rendered.

## Extension-first distribution regressions

::: {.need #TC-025 type="test-case" status="passed" tags="pytest;extension;distribution;provisioning;render" pytest-nodeid="tests/test_extension_first_distribution.py::test_a_clean_consumer_project_needs_no_engine_installation" evidenced-by="EVD-025"}
## Extension-first clean render

Render a real consumer project that has no installed package, no CLI on PATH, and no hand-authored pre-render, and verify the managed runtime is provisioned, the graph is produced, and cards and shortcodes resolve.
The starter also delegates to this bootstrap after Quarto installs its bundled extension with or without the GitHub owner namespace. `tests/test_extension_first_distribution.py::test_the_starter_template_needs_no_manual_activation_edit` renders both layouts.

## Coverage dashboard

The dashboard is computed from the same snapshot as the tables above. It reports each configured scope's coverage, the gaps behind those percentages, and the finding counts — the numbers `quarto-needs quality` enforces as gates in CI.

{{< need-dashboard id="verification-dashboard" >}}

A percentage here is not a claim that verification succeeded. `verification-trace` counts requirements that name a test case; `verification-successful` additionally requires that test to be passing, and `evidence` requires the chain to reach unexpired evidence. The distance between those three columns is the honest measure of assurance.
